clue.text: Intrude reformed characters into novel

indicators.note: the letters of the word Intrude are reformed, put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is told to push some rehabilitated criminals into the plot of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' rearranges the characters, the letters, of INTRUDE; 'characters into' links them to the definition. 'novel' is not a book here but an adjective: new.
explanation.definitionFit: Something novel is new and so not yet tested by experience.

clue.text: Sort of combat the peace-keepers are equipped for

parts.note: UN, the United Nations, sends peacekeeping forces
armed means equipped with weapons

explanation.surface: Someone asks what kind of fighting a peacekeeping force is kitted out for.
explanation.walkthrough: Ironic: the clue reads as UN ARMED, yet the answer means without weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Unarmed combat is fighting with bare hands and no weapons.

clue.text: Bird with sharp point on beak

parts.note: a thorn is a sharp point on a plant stem
a bird's beak is its bill

explanation.surface: A bird is described with a spike on its beak.
explanation.definitionFit: Thornbills are small Australian songbirds.

clue.text: Adult male needed in Shakespearian role

indicators.note: needed in says the male goes inside the role's name

parts.note: Iago is the villain of Shakespeare's Othello

explanation.surface: A grown man is wanted to play a part in a Shakespeare play.
explanation.definitionFit: An imago is the final, fully grown stage of an insect.

clue.text: Play the quick movements, showing exaggerated emotion

parts.note: a drama is a play
tics are quick involuntary twitches

explanation.surface: An actor overplays the twitchy bits of a role.
explanation.definitionFit: Dramatics is showy, overdone behaviour, like theatrical fuss.

clue.text: Device for putting juice in large dish

explanation.surface: Someone describes a gadget for pouring juice into a big plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'juice' is slang for electricity, so the device is a battery charger, not a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A battery charger puts electric power into a device; a charger is also an old word for a large flat serving platter.

clue.text: Stop up in Irish town talking

indicators.note: talking means the town's name is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: Cork is a city in the south of Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone is stuck in a town in Ireland, chatting.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech the two words rhyme, with no R sounded.
explanation.definitionFit: To caulk is to seal seams or gaps to make them watertight.

clue.text: Everyone's united round the Head of the Commonwealth suddenly

parts.note: all means everyone; the 's stands for is

indicators.note: round places the agreeing phrase around the next letter

parts.note: at one means in agreement, united

indicators.note: Head of picks the first letter of Commonwealth

explanation.surface: Everyone gathers round the Commonwealth's leader without warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of the Commonwealth' suggests the monarch; it is just C.
explanation.definitionFit: All at once means abruptly, without warning.

clue.text: Corgi got a bit of mutton

indicators.note: a bit of says the letters are a piece taken from within Corgi got

explanation.surface: A royal dog snatched a scrap of lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: The run straddles 'corGI GOT'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigot is a leg of lamb or sheep meat, prepared for roasting.

clue.text: Grasp sweetheart in broadcast serial

indicators.note: broadcast suggests scattering, so the letters of serial are spread into a new order

parts.note: the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: Someone hugs a loved one appearing in a TV drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' is not a lover: it means the heart of the word sweet, its middle letter. 'broadcast' makes REALIS from the serial's letters; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp an idea is to understand or become aware of it.

clue.text: In the past, an artist's market

parts.note: ago means in the past, as in 'years ago'
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist; the possessive joins him to the market

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a market that once belonged to a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: The agora was the open marketplace and meeting square of an ancient Greek city.

clue.text: Say, who's the French soldier with a flower?

parts.note: 'who's' said aloud is 'whose', and the French for whose (as in 'c'est à qui?') is à qui
le is the French masculine word for the
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Someone asks which French soldier is holding a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' tells you to hear 'who's' as 'whose', which French renders as à qui; the rest is a plain charade.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquilegia is the botanical genus of the columbine, a garden plant with spurred blooms.

clue.text: He discovered a shoddy area of land

parts.note: shoddy and mungo are both cloth made from recycled woollen rags, so one names the other
a park is an enclosed area of land, often public grounds

explanation.surface: Someone found a run-down plot of ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoddy' looks like an adjective for poor quality, but it is a noun: recycled wool cloth, also called MUNGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Mungo Park was the Scottish explorer who traced much of the course of the Niger River.

clue.text: Ice-cream without fruit for all

indicators.note: without signals that the second part of that ice cream's name is taken away

parts.note: tutti-frutti is an ice cream studded with candied fruit
frutti is Italian for fruits, the second half of that ice cream's name

explanation.surface: Someone offers everyone plain ice cream with no fruit in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove FRUTTI, the Italian 'fruit', from TUTTI-FRUTTI.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the direction tutti marks a passage played by the whole ensemble together.

clue.text: Pub with leading entertainer shows lively spirit

indicators.note: leading means the entertainer goes in front of the pub

parts.note: a DJ, disc jockey, entertains by playing records
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A bar with a headline act boasts of its lively atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: A djinn is a spirit of Arabic folklore, often mischievous and powerful.

clue.text: Pole going to ground has a narrow escape

parts.note: N is the North Pole
earthing is connecting a circuit to the ground

explanation.surface: An electric pole is earthed and narrowly avoids disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A near thing is a close shave or a narrow escape.

clue.text: Article is a fashionable plate

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
a dental plate holding false teeth is a denture

explanation.surface: A newspaper item claims a certain dish is in vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plate' is not crockery but a set of false teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Articles, as of apprenticeship, are a formal contract binding one party to serve another.

clue.text: Cashier's acquittal

explanation.surface: A bank teller is cleared in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cashier' is a verb, to dismiss from the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge is to dismiss, as to cashier an officer; a discharge is also a release from a charge.

clue.text: She puts you in your place, being a school-marm?

definitions.text: She puts you in your place, being a school-marm?

parts.words: She puts you in your place, being a school-marm?
parts.note: a female attendant at a theatre or cinema shows you to your seat; the question mark hints at a female version of a junior school teacher, once called an usher

explanation.surface: A strict schoolmistress keeps pupils in line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts you in your place' sounds like a scolding but is literal: seating you at the cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinema attendants who show patrons to seats were women in such roles.

clue.text: Firm pound slides, then falls

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
L stands for the pound sterling, from Latin libra
lapses means slides into a worse state

explanation.surface: A company reports the pound weakening, then dropping sharply.
explanation.definitionFit: To collapse is to fall down or give way suddenly.

clue.text: Share bill with daughter for apple tree

parts.note: to co-star is to share top billing

explanation.surface: A performer shares a poster with their daughter for an orchard.
explanation.definitionFit: Costard is an old English variety of large cooking apple.

clue.text: Distinctive character of Barnet hospital

indicators.note: of signals the letters are taken from within the words Barnet hospital

explanation.surface: A local hospital in the north London suburb of Barnet is praised for its special atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: BARNET is a London borough; the run sits across 'BarnET HOSpital'.
explanation.definitionFit: The spirit or guiding beliefs of a community or institution form its ethos.

clue.text: Be sulky, changing colour

indicators.note: changing says the letters of Be sulky are moved into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stop sulking and shifting their colouring.
explanation.definitionFit: Sky blue is a pale clear shade like a cloudless sky.

clue.text: Disruption in Croatian port

explanation.surface: Trouble breaks out at a harbour on the Adriatic.
explanation.definitionFit: A split is a rupture or division in a group; Split is also the large port city on Croatia's Dalmatian coast.

clue.text: Fault in the sound circuits

indicators.note: the sound says the word for circuits is heard, giving a word spoken alike

parts.note: laps are circuits of a track

explanation.surface: A defect is found in the circuitry of a hi-fi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like audio but signals a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a slip or minor error.

clue.text: Like Arnold's gypsy, shall cry out about nothing

indicators.note: about places those mixed letters around the next piece
out says the letters of shall cry are knocked into a new order

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Someone says a wandering traveller in a poem will shout over trifles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cry out' looks like one phrase but 'cry' is fodder. Matthew Arnold wrote the Victorian poem 'The Scholar-Gipsy', so his gypsy is scholarly.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnold's poem calls its wanderer a scholar, so being learned and studious fits him.

clue.text: One who needs a couple of sticks when going downhill

definitions.text: One who needs a couple of sticks when going downhill

parts.words: One who needs a couple of sticks when going downhill
parts.note: suggests someone frail on walking sticks, but describes a sportsperson on the slopes with two poles

explanation.surface: An elderly person needs two canes as their health declines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going downhill' hints at failing health; it is literal, on snow.
explanation.definitionFit: A person on skis carries two poles for balance on a slope.

clue.text: Motorway is illuminated round the perimeter

indicators.note: round says the word for illuminated goes around the motorway letter

parts.note: lit means illuminated
MI, read as M1, is Britain's first motorway, from London to Leeds

explanation.surface: A motorway is lit up along its edges.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the main British motorway north from London; crosswords write it with the letter I for the figure 1.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit is a boundary or outer edge.

clue.text: It makes more noise if one's in a more spacious setting

indicators.note: in tells us the conditional word and the numeral go inside the next word

parts.note: ampler means roomier, more spacious
I is the Roman numeral one; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A sound system is said to be louder when placed in a bigger room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' and 'setting' are links: 'setting' frames the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An audio amp boosts a signal so the sound is louder.

clue.text: Ran into a line of stones in the road

parts.note: met means encountered, ran into someone

explanation.surface: Someone stumbled on a row of cobbles in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: Road metal is broken stone used to build roads, a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken stone laid as road foundation is called road metal.

clue.text: Sprinkler that clears the bed

explanation.surface: A garden device that also tidies the flower bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed is a river bed, and the sprinkler shakes flour or sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: A dredger is a kitchen shaker for dusting flour; it is also a vessel that scoops silt from a riverbed.

clue.text: Going to great lengths to be outrageous

explanation.surface: Someone travels far just to cause a scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme means farthest out or most drastic, and also beyond reasonable bounds.
